title: Customer Advocacy Intake Queue and Weighted Commitment Model
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Create a repeatable, auditable intake queue and a transparent weighted-commitment model (Advocacy Score) to prioritize inbound requests from top accounts and escalations so we can make predictable roadmap commitments. Scope: intake form + automated queue, scoring algorithm + explainability, triage rules for automated vs. high-touch lanes, SLAs for acknowledgement and decision, dashboard for PM/AE/CS alignment. Out of scope for this ticket: implementation of full automation for non-top-account channels (follow-up ticket planned). Background: multiple recent escalations from strategic customers have created ad hoc prioritization decisions and missed SLAs. Sales and CS need a predictable runway and clear commitments. We will pilot with three strategic accounts and the top-accounts escalation channel before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria: An intake form (Confluence + Zendesk/Gainsight webhook) that captures required attributes and auto-calculates an Advocacy Score
Advocacy Score algorithm defined and documented with weight breakdown and rationales
Automated queue in Redwood Intake Board that routes items into: low-touch backlog, high-touch review, or immediate escalation
SLA configuration: acknowledgement < 24 hours for top accounts; decision or runway proposal < 10 business days for high-touch requests
Pilot with 3 accounts completed and feedback captured; at least one ticket processed through engineering handoff
PM/AE/CS dashboard tile showing queue size, average score, decision latency, and predicted commitment runway

decisions: Pilot with 3 accounts before company-wide rollout to validate scoring thresholds
Use percentage weights for scoring with an explicit tie-breaker 'time-to-impact' field
Engineering effort to be t-shirt-sized then normalized to points to limit estimation overhead
Automated routing only for unambiguous low-touch requests; anything with compliance/regulatory flag goes to high-touch review
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot, 2 weeks): deploy intake form and webhook; manual review for high-touch lane; collect feedback. Phase 2 (Automation, 3 weeks): automation rules for routing and dashboard tile; engineering handoffs as normal tickets. Phase 3 (Scale, 2 sprints): iterate on weights, add Gainsight integration and SLA monitoring. Communicate cadence and SLA to Sales/CS and update playbook.
metrics: % of top-account requests with decision within 10 business days (target: >= 85%)
Median time to first response for top accounts (target: < 24 hours)
% of pilot requests accurately classified (manual audit) (target: >= 90%)
Number of roadmap commitments made vs delivered (quarterly commit accuracy target: 80%)
CS satisfaction score on intake process (post-pilot survey target: >= 4/5)
implementation_notes: Intake webhook payload should include raw fields and computed Advocacy Score for auditability
Store score components in metadata for explainability in the Console (so PMs can see why a request scored high)
Dashboard tile will surface 'predicted runway' calculated from score + current backlog velocity (ENG-4231 dependency)
Prefer server-side calculation to avoid client-side manipulation; include versioning for score algorithm
Fallback policy: if scoring service unavailable, mark item 'manual triage required' and notify triage owner
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting weights to pilot accounts. Mitigation: Re-evaluate weights after pilot and run A/B on different weight sets in the next cycle.
Risk: Political push from Sales to bypass queue. Mitigation: Escalation governance doc and single executive tie-breaker for exceptions.
Risk: Engineering capacity mismatch. Mitigation: Surface predicted runway and require cost-benefit justification for any expedited work.
Risk: Score explainability concerns with customers. Mitigation: Keep score internal and provide human-readable rationale when committing.
Risk: Automation misroutes urgent compliance requests. Mitigation: Any request with compliance flag auto-routes to high-touch and triggers 4-hour ack for security team
